input_scope: Only listed manager runs starting Oct 24-26; weather base files AND rotated parts. No audit/process/order/Redis/Catalog reads.
ordering: received_ns when positive, else recorded_at_ns. Exact integer nanoseconds; sorted; source JSON bytes preserved under record.
success_definition: metar_poll with a nonempty rows array means a logged response, NOT verified successful strategy processing or trading.
replay_rules: Treat local received_ns as the earliest captured weather availability; never inject a row at its older obsTime or AWC receiptTime.
Retain source run_id/event_id and metar_delivered timestamps; strict strategy timing also requires the live processed_ns, not just HTTP receipt.
Do not deduplicate repeated polls, fill historical gaps, carry state across run boundaries without matching the live lifecycle, or merge adjacent Event dates.
Some polls on Oct 25/26 target next-day Events; preserve event_id rather than assigning an Event from the receipt date.
Historical error records may use a pre-request received_ns in this poller; keep recorded_at_ns and the original error, not a synthetic response time.
For L2 alignment use a comparable local receive clock (or disclose exchange-time-only clock uncertainty); never consume future L2 snapshots.
limitations: No statement that the two days were fully healthy/live-trading; current systemctl/health cannot establish this.
Rows describing earlier weather in a late response do not establish that live knew those observations earlier.
No native-weather normalization or execution engine was run; no fill/non-fill claim checked.
Input scope is the existing manager weather journals, not every possible historical data location.
